pourquoiQuitte.introTexte: Twenty questions about the last months of your relationship. There's no right answer: answer based on what was happening, not on what you wish had happened.
pourquoiQuitte.resultatLibelle: What weighed the most in the breakup
pourquoiQuitte.axe_projets: Not the same life, not the same pace
pourquoiQuitte.p_flamme_d: Based on your answers, what weighed the most was wear and tear: less desire, fewer moments just for the two of you, and the feeling of living side by side rather than together. It's no one's fault in particular, it's what happens when everyday life takes up all the room and you stop making time for each other.
pourquoiQuitte.p_flamme_a: If you're hoping for a comeback, know that a spark rarely relights on its own: you'd both have to change the way you live together. For next time, remember one simple thing: time together needs protecting, even when everything's going well.
pourquoiQuitte.p_flamme_c: The spark had faded little by little under everyday life.
pourquoiQuitte.p_eloignement_d: Your answers are mostly about distance: each with your own life, things you stopped telling each other, one of you feeling alone even as a couple. Nothing dramatic, and that's exactly why people rarely see it coming. One day, one of you realizes there isn't much left between you.
pourquoiQuitte.p_eloignement_a: This kind of breakup often leaves a feeling of something unfinished, because there was no "big reason". Next time, keep the habit of talking about what's wrong before the silence settles in.
pourquoiQuitte.p_eloignement_c: You had drifted apart, without really noticing.
pourquoiQuitte.p_conflits_t: The arguments had worn everything down
pourquoiQuitte.p_conflits_d: Your answers talk about arguments that kept coming back, blame and words that hurt. Over time, a relationship can wear out even when there's still love. It's not arguing that wears a couple down, it's the way you do it: contempt and repeated criticism do far more damage than the disagreements themselves.
pourquoiQuitte.p_conflits_a: If a comeback is possible, it will take a different way of talking to each other, not just apologies. And for you, next time, learn to spot the moment when a discussion turns into an attack: that's when you need to take a break.
pourquoiQuitte.p_conflits_c: The repeated arguments also weighed a lot.
pourquoiQuitte.p_projets_t: You didn't want the same life
pourquoiQuitte.p_projets_d: Based on your answers, you weren't heading in the same direction, or not at the same pace: one wanted to commit, move in or have a baby, the other backed off. This kind of breakup is often the hardest to accept, because there's sometimes still a lot of love. But love isn't enough when you don't want the same life.
pourquoiQuitte.p_projets_a: Don't tell yourself you "asked for too much": wanting plans isn't excessive. What you need is someone who wants them too. And if your ex comes back, first ask yourself whether their plans have changed.
pourquoiQuitte.p_projets_c: You weren't heading toward the same life either, or not at the same pace.
pourquoiQuitte.p_etouffement_d: Your answers talk about jealousy, texts at all hours, needing reassurance. Your ex probably felt smothered, and leaving ended up seeming like the only way to breathe. That doesn't make you a toxic person: it's often the fear of losing someone that makes us hold on too tight.
pourquoiQuitte.p_etouffement_a: This may be the most useful result for the future. Needing constant reassurance often comes from a way of attaching to people that you can work on, on your own or with a professional. And next time, leave room for the other person: it's often what makes them stay.
pourquoiQuitte.p_confiance_d: Your answers talk about lies, secrets or things kept to yourselves, on one side or the other. Once trust is broken, every detail becomes suspicious, and the relationship ends up worn out from checking, doubting or hiding.
pourquoiQuitte.p_confiance_a: Trust can be rebuilt, but not with promises: with actions, over time. If your ex comes back, it's the first thing to look at. And if the lies came from you, ask yourself what was stopping you from saying things.
pourquoiQuitte.p_confiance_c: Trust had also been damaged between you.
pourquoiQuitte.p_autre_t: Someone else had come into their life
pourquoiQuitte.p_autre_d: Based on your answers, there's a good chance another person played a part in the breakup: habits that change, a phone that gets hidden, a sudden breakup, a new relationship very quickly. It hurts, and it often leaves you feeling replaced. Yet the new person often shows up when the relationship was already going less well.
pourquoiQuitte.p_autre_a: Don't go looking in yourself for what was "missing": your ex made a choice, and it's theirs. Cut contact while you heal, especially with their social media, that's what hurts the most right now.
pourquoiQuitte.p_autre_c: Someone else may also have played a part.
pourquoiQuitte.p_moment_d: Your answers talk about an ex who wasn't doing well: stress, studies, a job that took everything, questioning their life, maybe grief or depression. At times like that, some people no longer have the strength to carry a relationship, even with someone they love. For once, "it's not you, it's me" may have been true.
pourquoiQuitte.p_moment_a: Don't stay hanging on the hope that they'll get better and come back: you can't get better for them. Take care of yourself first. If your ex comes back one day, it'll be up to them to make the first move.
pourquoiQuitte.p_moment_c: Your ex was also going through a hard time.
pourquoiQuitte.p_ouvert_d: No cause really stands out in your answers. Your breakup looks more like a pile-up of small things: a bit of wear and tear, a bit of distance, a few disagreements. That's often the case, and it's also why it's so hard to explain why it's over.
pourquoiQuitte.p_ouvert_a: Look at the two or three highest causes above: together, they probably tell your story better than a single reason would. And don't look for someone to blame, there often isn't one.
